claims.text: A machine-learning model can integrate ab initio mode-specific phonon features with composition data for screening high-entropy alloys.
The integrated model will predict low phonon thermal conductivity more accurately than models based on simplified averaged descriptors.
The target HEAs have complex, multicomponent disordered microstructures.
The target HEAs are intended for thermal-insulation applications.
Phonon transport dominates heat conduction from ambient to moderately elevated temperatures in the target HEAs.
Configurational disorder in multielement HEAs produces complex phonon-scattering mechanisms.
Mode-specific phonon lifetimes, group velocities, and scattering rates capture the vibrational dynamics governing heat conduction in disordered alloys.
Using mode-specific phonon parameters allows a model to resolve contributions from different phonon modes more accurately than averaged or empirical descriptors.
The integrated model will produce a statistically significant reduction in prediction error.
The mean prediction error will be reduced by approximately 20% or more relative to current models.
Current predictive approaches use empirical or simplified theoretical descriptors of phonon scattering and composition-conductivity correlations.
The approach will be most effective for compositions and operating conditions represented in its training data.
Model accuracy may diminish for alloys undergoing phase transformations.
Model accuracy may diminish for alloys with extreme disorder not represented by the ab initio descriptors.
The quantitative improvement depends on the quality of the ab initio vibrational data.
The quantitative improvement depends on the representativeness of the training set.
Experimental validation is needed to establish the model's accuracy and applicability limits.
Phonon thermal conductivity can be benchmarked experimentally using time-domain thermoreflectance or an equivalent technique.
Failure to reduce mean prediction error by about 20% relative to conventional models would falsify the hypothesis.
Failure of model-selected alloys to exhibit statistically lower measured conductivity than alloys selected by standard approaches would falsify the hypothesis.
